Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1310 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player.
  • Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.
  • Sources indicate that he trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player.

Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.

Sources indicate that he trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.

According to recent reports, “We’ll do maybe two days on, one day off, and then three days on, one day off,” states Peters. “We’ve been doing that for just over a year now. It’s full-on. It’s pretty much as if you were at a club.”.

In a recent development, dele rose as a teenager to a level of stardom few experience and, used to media attention, doesn’t mind that his absence from football draws scrutiny. But he disagrees with the suggestion that choosing to stream on Twitch is a sign he has lost interest in the game that made him wealthy enough to never need to work again.

To a modest Twitch audience, he sometimes plays video games, sometimes just talks. He has a knack for creating viral content, sharing a phone call with Harry Kane and playing a game of EA Sports FC with IShowSpeed, one of the most famous online influencers. When he lost that game – and a bet – he wore an Arsenal shirt, apologising to Spurs fans before burning it. When TalkSport pundits claimed Dele was wasting his potential by becoming a streamer, Dele responded in a live stream, pointing out he was recording himself in his spare time and if he was out at nightclubs, it would be worse. Even then he was polite.

According to recent reports, “When people see him online streaming or whatever he does in his private time, the initial thought is: ‘He’s done with football, then,’” Peters claims. “He’s been training for a year and a half by himself. If he was done with football he wouldn’t be doing that. His actions show that the hunger is still there. A lot of people would come out of the game and then stop and lose the hunger for it, but he’s still chipping away every day, trying to get back and get to somewhere that he’s happy with.”.

Dele broke through at MK Dons as a slight but devilish defensive midfielder, dominating League One midfields full of hardened professionals, before being scouted by Tottenham. Mauricio Pochettino attended MK Dons’ 4-0 League Cup win against Manchester United in 2014 and saw enough to leave early and convince Daniel Levy to pay £5m.

Recent findings suggest that by the time Dele turned 21, his statistics were superior to Cristiano Ronaldo’s at the same age: 26 goals and 14 assists to Ronaldo’s 14 and 13. His 40 goal involvements equalled Frank Lampard, Steven Gerrard and David Beckham combined at the same age.

In a recent development, “He’s scored more in his first 50 league games than Steven Gerrard, Wayne Rooney and Frank Lampard,” Pochettino wrote in his book Brave Fresh World. “He may go on to be better than all of them because he has the quality; now he just needs consistency.”.

But there were, perhaps, warning signs of what would happen at Spurs. One source who worked closely with Dele describes him as a “cheeky chappy”; charming and universally popular.

Industry observers note that he wasn’t one to miss training, but there were concerns he wasn’t leading the pristine lifestyle of many elite players, and tabloid stories about his private life trailed him. Pochettino was concerned when he saw Dele’s WhatsApp photo, a cartoon of a boy surrounded by people wanting a piece of him, believing he needed support from the right people. John McDermott, the head of coaching and development, remarked: “When the trough is full, the pigs come from all over to feed.”.

In a recent development, when Dele voluntarily liquidated one of his companies this month, documents highlighted an estimated surplus after costs of £7.6m, suggesting the 30-year-old has not squandered the millions he earned at his peak in wages and sponsorship agreements, including a five-year deal with Adidas. He also owns a property portfolio worth more than £1.5m.

In the early days Pochettino warned Dele about the danger of not giving maximum effort in matches and training, a sentiment later shared by José Mourinho when he became Spurs manager. “I think one day you will regret, if you don’t reach what you can reach,” Mourinho told Dele in his office as Amazon Prime’s cameras rolled.

Sources indicate that although Dele formed a formidable relationship with Kane on the pitch, and was twice named the Professional Footballers’ Association’s men’s young player of the year while playing behind the striker, he was closer to Eric Dier off it. And perhaps it was those anchors – Pochettino and Dier – that Dele lost later in his career.

Recent findings suggest that his time with Pochettino was fondly remembered. For the Argentinian’s 50th birthday celebrations, Dele recorded a heartfelt video for his former manager. “The message was beautiful,” indicates one party-goer.

In almost five years since leaving Spurs, he has made one league start at Everton and 10 at Besiktas, before a loan at Como, where Cesc Fàbregas tried to rediscover the player he once was. He came off the bench once and was sent off nine minutes later.

Recent findings suggest that dele, according to those close to him, is biding his time to get his next move right. He will be 31 in April and wants a suitable contract. He has spoken to a host of clubs, with interest from the Premier League and the Championship, and from the Middle East, where he has been tempted by the riches of the Saudi Pro League, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar. There has also been interest from Major League Soccer and he has held talks with clubs in Brazil and Japan. It is believed he will join a club this season.

In a recent development, in preparation, Peters is also guiding Dele’s nutrition, though he does not require much guidance. “Del’s a weird one, because he doesn’t snack, he doesn’t eat unhealthily, he doesn’t have a Sprite or a Coke or whatever. He’s never really been that kind of guy. All he does is drink coconut water, and he’ll have a small lunch, or his cheat day will be a Nando’s or something.”.

Happiness is his priority. He spoke candidly on Gary Neville’s The Overlap in 2023 about his struggles with mental health and an addiction to sleeping pills after revealing abuse as a child. “Because he’s had such a long time out, he’s like: ‘What’s another few months if it means that I’m going to find something I’m actually happy with?’” Peters says. The aim is to “carry on for as long as possible”.

For the time being, Dele’s days are simple. When not training, he goes for coffee or a swim, and he has taken up padel. “He’s very much a person that’s happy with the little things,” Peters says. “He’s always the person that’s positive, the one that, if the group’s down or whatever, is going to pick everyone up. He’s happy with what he’s doing. His main happiness is playing football, and that’s what he wants to do.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"3 Body Problem," Netflix's unsettling adaptation of the first book in Chinese author Cixin Liu's epic alien invasion trilogy, "Remembrance of Earth’s Past," made a serious impact on viewers searching for hardcore E.T. drama and now an explosive upcoming trailer for season 2 has just entered our orbit.

Recent findings suggest that this sensational saga about a malevolent interstellar society trying to exist within the unpredictable orbital mechanics of a planet and its triple sun system that forms an Earth-bound armada still has us a bit slack-jawed more than two years after debuting in 2024. Now we're admittedly eager for this shortened 6-episode sophomore outing, which is officially arriving on Jan. 14, 2027.

Industry observers note that delivered by Emmy Award-winning "Game of Thrones" team of David Benioff and D.B. Weiss and "True Blood's" Alexander Woo, "3 Body Problem" season 2 revolves around the combined forces of the Planetary Defense Council as they mount a daring deep space counterattack against the San-Ti.

These Trisolarians are not the friendliest of galactic neighbors, and prior to the all-out invasion their primary goal was to thwart humanity’s ability to create advanced defense weaponry in the four centuries it would take for them to enter our solar system. This time it's more about the next phase of ultimate survival and dire actions taken by anti-alien and pro-alien factions.

Season 2 leaps forward 400 years and focuses on the results of the Wallfacer Project, a secret initiative where chosen individuals worked on solutions in isolation as to not attract the attention of the Trisolarian's omnipresent AI surveillance technology called sophons.

While the debut season was based on Liu's Hugo Award-winning 2008 novel, "The Three-Body Problem," this upcoming Netflix offering will adapt the second book, "The Dark Forest." 2010's "Death's End" closed out the acclaimed sci-fi trilogy.

"So much of season 1 is about the mystery of what's happening," co-creator and co-executive producer David Benioff tells Netflix. "By the time season 2 starts, we have a lot more information. We know there is a hostile alien civilization out there, the San-Ti, and they’re coming our way, and they want our planet for themselves.".

Landing on Jan. 14, 2027, "3 Body Problem" season 2's international cast includes returners Jess Hong, Benedict Wong, Jovan Adepo, Eiza González, Liam Cunningham, Marlo Kelly, Sea Shimooka, Saamer Usmani, Alex Sharp and Josh Brener. Joining them are fresh cast members Claudia Doumit, Ellie de Lange, Alfie Allen, David Yip and Jordan Sunshine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Man accused of abusing former Bournemouth winger.

Alleged incident happened at Anfield game in 2025.

A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the Manchester City forward withdrew his support for the prosecution.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool magistrates court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the Premier League match between Liverpool and Semenyo’s former club Bournemouth at Anfield on 15 August last year.

But Simon Jones, prosecuting, mentioned: “Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him. In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.”.

District judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

Semenyo, who left Bournemouth for Manchester City in January, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mogan was taken to hospital after a seizure.

Sources indicate that the court had heard Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted racial abuse at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game. He was alleged to have noted: “Hurry up and take the throw-in, you black bastard.”.

Recent findings suggest that opening the case last month, Mr Jones noted: “That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him. Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn’t believe what the male had said.”.

In a recent development, mogan then shouted: “I’m talking to you, you cunt,” the court heard. Witnesses also said they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.

In a recent development, semenyo reported the incident to the referee and Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time. Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to “hurry up”.

Mogan declined to comment as he left court.

Latest Update: Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.
  • "There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak said after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.
  • "The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.

"There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak said after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.

"The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".

The threat comes after the Canadian government confirmed Wednesday that it would not allow Russian players to take part in the IIHF World Junior Championship starting on December 26 in Alberta.

Recent findings suggest that "Canada's position is unequivocal: as long as Russia continues ⁠its war of aggression ​against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual," Adam van Koeverden, Canada's secretary of sport, said in a statement on Wednesday. "Canada will continue to stand with Ukraine.".

Following the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling in late October, in which it said the security concerns the IIHF cited for barring Russian teams from taking part in international tournaments was not sufficient, the world governing body pledged to work to comply with the decision.

On November 8, Norway remarked it had been bumped from the World Juniors tournament and had been informed by the IIHF that Russia would take its place. Several other national hockey associations said they had received a revised schedule for the tournament and stated they would not play against Russia. The IIHF has not confirmed the change.

Germany has been watching developments related to the World Juniors and host nation Canada closely, as it is set to host the IIHF World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf starting on May 14.

With several nations saying they will not play Russia and major sponsors threatening to pull out, a German government spokesman described the prospect of hosting the tournament under these conditions as "effectively impossible.".

However, Germany has ruled out taking the Canadian approach.

Ronald Rauhe, Germany's minister of state for sport, remarked Wednesday that refusing to grant visas was "not a solution for the [German] ice hockey federation [DEB], nor is it a solution for successfully hosting a world championship anywhere.".

At the same time, though, he expressed support for the DEB in its wish to host the tournament as planned.

"We believe that we should channel all our energy and efforts into helping sport — and ice hockey in particular — find a solution, which would, of course, entail excluding Russia from the World Championship.".

What makes things even more complicated for German officials are concerns that taking a hard-line on Russia could jeopardize Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

The thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees bidding to host an Olympic Games to follow its lead. The IOC is set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process.

It has been revealed that for now, though, the ball appears to be in the IIHF's court, after Ottawa confirmed its refusal to grant Russians visas to play in the World Juniors. How the dispute regarding that tournament gets resolved could go a long way to finding a solution for the men's tournament in Germany in May.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy.

Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better".

Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international mentioned he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".

Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness mentioned earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had".

The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned, external the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested, external the deal may need to be renegotiated.

"Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," remarked a Fifpro statement., external.

It has been revealed that "In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.".

Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness.

Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala?

Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September.

He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist.

Sources indicate that "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

According to recent reports, "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

It has been revealed that "Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.".

Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months".

NFL legend was Chelsea guest at Club World Cup.

Tom Brady is in discussions about buying a small stake in Chelsea. The NFL legend sold a minority share in Birmingham City this month after three years, a move sources remarked was to pave the way for investing at Stamford Bridge.

Brady was a guest of Chelsea when they won the Club World Cup in Upcoming Jersey last year and was seen celebrating with the players after their remarkable 3-0 final win over Paris Saint-Germain.

The seven-time Super Bowl winner is understood to have a good relationship with Behdad Eghbali, whose fund, Clearlake Capital, owns 86.5% of Chelsea after Todd Boehly and Mark Walter sold their shares in September.

Brady bought into Birmingham in August 2023, less than a year after his second and final retirement from the NFL, after the club’s takeover by Tom Wagner’s Knighthead Capital.

Brady was appointed chair of the club’s advisory board and had a prominent role in the 2025 Amazon Prime documentary Built in Birmingham: Brady & The Blues, which made headlines when he questioned the “work ethic” of Wayne Rooney, who was the manager.

In announcing Brady’s departure the club mentioned: “Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.”.

Brady owns a minority stake in the NFL team Las Vegas Raiders, which he purchased alongside Wagner.

Hirst key for Stoke, injuries derail Millwall - Sam Parkin's EFL takeaways

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After the last international break of the year, Final Score pundit and former Swindon Town, Luton Town and Northampton Town striker selects his takeaways from the Championship, League One and League Two.
  • Stoke City are the Championship's form team, having taken 32 points from the last 39, but can they stay the distance in the promotion race?
  • Parkin: "I think everyone, probably me included, is really optimistic about their chances of this being the season they get it right.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After the last international break of the year, Final Score pundit and former Swindon Town, Luton Town and Northampton Town striker selects his takeaways from the Championship, League One and League Two.

Stoke City are the Championship's form team, having taken 32 points from the last 39, but can they stay the distance in the promotion race?

Parkin: "I think everyone, probably me included, is really optimistic about their chances of this being the season they get it right.

According to recent reports, "We're a fair chunk into the season now and I thought today's result was really important because I believe this was their first win over anyone in the top eight. It felt like a bit of a statement win because Birmingham, apart from their defeat at Cardiff, have been really competitive in more or less every game.

"They've been able to just come out the right side of the scoreline and they've had to rely on their goalkeeper [Viktor] Johansson, who I think is one of the top goalkeepers at this level.

"I think there was an early shift in formation, going to a back three in the early part of the campaign, and I think that's proved quite notable. They're keeping clean sheets and they've got a goalscorer in George Hirst.

Industry observers note that "I read a lot about Stoke City fans saying they're still probably short on forwards who are going to get them the goals. I know that [Jack] McGlynn has chipped in with a really impressive number from midfield, but for Hirst to get that massive winning goal, that will have done his confidence the world of good.

"He's been promoted previously with Ipswich and there's no reason why he can't be Stoke's main man up front.".

Dejected Millwall boss Alex Neil.

Millwall have slumped to 16th after fighting for promotion in the last few seasons and they have lost five of their last seven league games.

Parkin: "They've had to deal with a horrendous injury crisis. It was at a level that I was struggling to think of a comparable club in the early part of the season. They were just having players go down week after week.

"There was one game in particular I covered against Wrexham and they had the walking wounded (out there), so I think they're still recovering from that.

"They've got some of the main players in [Casper] De Norre back fit now and available, but I think [Josh] Coburn was unavailable again today, and [Mihailo] Ivanovic is just making his way back - I would say they are three of their more notable players.

"Take away [Jake] Cooper at the back, who's been a mainstay for a number of years, and I think that trio I've just mentioned are so fundamental to their chances this season.

"They're still playing catch up to a degree, but Alex Neil has not pulled any punches in some of his interviews and he'll be disappointed.

"On the flip side of that, QPR are in a really good place at the moment, and are a much tougher proposition than maybe they would have been over the last couple of seasons.

Industry observers note that "I think Millwall will improve over time. I don't see them emulating what they did last season, but I think they can be optimistic they can get some better results once everyone's back available.".

Lincoln City management duo Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

Lincoln City are finding life in the Championship tough after romping to the League One title last season and they have lost seven of their last nine league games.

Industry observers note that parkin: "It's been a downward spiral and the home form's a bit of an concern. They just have the one win over Burnley there - and Burnley were in dire straits when they came.

"They've lost four in a row so that will be a little bit of a concern because they found a formula on the road in the early part of the season. But, yeah, you've got to do better in your home form.

"I still trust they're going to be competitive and the majority of that squad, Jack Moylan apart, is still there from last season. You don't get over 100 points and then lose everything.

"That's always going to count for something when you've got the nucleus of that squad still together, even if it is in a higher division. So I think the spirit will remain amongst that group, despite the recent defeats.

"They've got to start taking points off the better teams in the division as well. All their victories have come against teams who are in the lower part of the table, like Preston and Burnley.

"They won at Bolton and at Bristol City, so they're not really mixing it with the teams in the top half of the table at the moment.

"But I think the bottom line is the management duo would have absolutely taken being five points above 22nd at this stage of the season, so they've given themselves a good opportunity to stay in the division.".

Glum Barnsley boss Daniel Stendel.

Barnsley are four points from safety at the bottom of League One after Friday's defeat by Sheffield Wednesday in the South Yorkshire derby and are on course for a first return to the fourth tier since 1979.

In a recent development, parkin: "I think on last night's evidence, they're a better team than the league table suggests. That's an absolute certainty in my mind.

It has been revealed that "My one concern is where are the goals going to come from? For all their dangerous play, which is incredibly aggressive and energetic, with and without the ball, where are the goals?

"They throw caution to the wind and there's a real energy and youth about the side, which I actually really admired in defeat.

"It's just translating all that into goals and that was obviously one part of it against Wednesday, and giving away bad goals - they've conceded the most set pieces now in the division.

In a recent development, "They conceded in that manner again, and because they play such a high line, they (also) get exposed by teams on the counter. Maybe that's a little bit of naivety. Maybe that's a little bit lack of experience, which they can go some way to mending in January when the transfer window opens.

In a recent development, "But they may be adrift at the bottom if they don't turn things around soon. In short, I think they're a better team than a relegated team. But the most important thing in football, as we know, is putting the ball in the back of the net and that clearly is a problem for them at the moment.".

Crawley Town's Dylan Morgan celebrates scoring against Cheltenham Town.

Crawley Town boosted their chances of staying in the EFL when they recorded their first home league win of the season over Fleetwood Town and they have generated some momentum in their last few matches.

Parkin: "Former Leeds and Sheffield United manager Kevin Blackwell is in charge now till the end of the season. I was injured for the majority of his spell at Luton Town when he was my manager, but I'm kind of well versed in his methods and he will make them really hard to beat.

Industry observers note that "That's always the first thing you want when you take over a struggling side, you need to stop shipping goals. You need to get them organised. You need to work on set-pieces and be a threat on that front. He will do all those things.

According to recent reports, "I think the three results in the league, two wins and a draw, have indicated you that his methods have already come to fruition. His approach will be very different to probably what the players were being asked to do under Scott Lindsey.

It has been revealed that "It'll be a different kind of football. They'll play long at times, they'll want to play in the opposition's half. I think in terms of a blueprint to get survival, he could very well be the man to supply that.

"They've chosen him after he was initially brought in as interim manager because the performances have improved across the last few weeks, despite the embarrassment of the FA Cup defeat to Wimborne.

"He's made them competitive very swiftly and I think a lot of teams are going to be in for a real game when they face them.".

Sam Parkin was speaking to BBC Sport England's David Anderson.

#70885. Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon tonight

Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon tonight

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (404 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset tonight (Nov.
  • Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S.
  • Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset tonight (Nov. 20), presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby.

Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length.

Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.

Industry observers note that the moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior.

Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant, along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025.

Depending on viewing conditions, you may also notice a shoal of bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk, which represent the large moons Titan, Dione, Tethys, Rhea and Iapetus.

In a recent development, interested in seeing the planets of the solar system up close for yourself? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes available in 2026, including the Celestron NexStar 8SE, which we rate as the best motorized scope out there.

Editor's Note: If you would like to share your planetary astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

Anthony Wood joined Space.com in April 2025 after contributing articles to outlets including IGN, New Atlas and Gizmodo. He has a passion for the night sky, science, Hideo Kojima, and human space exploration, and can’t wait for the day when astronauts once again set foot on the moon.

Premier League news: Moyes demands more from Grealish, Iraola wary of United threat

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everton’s playmaker returns after being stood down, while Liverpool’s head coach keeps focus for Anfield showdown.
  • David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad.
  • Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton’s playmaker returns after being stood down, while Liverpool’s head coach keeps focus for Anfield showdown.

David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad.

Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October but he is fit and available for Monday’s visit to Brentford.

“He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before,” the Everton manager said. “We will get on with things. The team is doing really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.”.

The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week andalso apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who won three of four matches in his absence. Grealish, however, had struggled to replicate last season’s form impact when joining on loan from Manchester City prior to his breach of discipline. And Moyes is demanding more.

He added: “Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, more goals. There’s lots of things about him which we need and he’s good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need. I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we’re hoping to get that again.”.

The Everton manager has backed Jordan Pickford to respond strongly to the threat from James Trafford to his England place, following after the Leeds goalkeeper’s inclusion and impressive display in the Nations League win over Spain.

Industry observers note that “I don’t think it will have a great effect on him,” claimed Moyes. “If you’re playing for England you will always have other players chasing you. I still think Jordan Pickford is out there on his own at the moment. If anything, he’s getting better. It will be good for us now that he’s getting competition [with England].” Andy Hunter.

Andoni Iraola has noted Liverpool must disregard the latest turmoil at Manchester United and treat Sunday’s visitors like the team that thrived under Michael Carrick last season.

According to recent reports, sunday will be the first time since March 1937 that United have faced Liverpool in a league game at Anfield while languishing in the relegation zone. Mauricio Pochettino could start his United reign bottom of the table should results on Saturday go against his latest club.

It has been revealed that iraola never lost in six league meetings with United as Bournemouth head coach. Before his first taste of the fixture with Liverpool, he insisted his north-west rivals are in a false position.

Industry observers note that “United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season,” Iraola said. “Now we have just started, it is just 10 games. For sure, they will be a lot higher in the table [soon]. We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

In a recent development, “We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a substantial game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, this is the biggest one in English football, so we want to play well and we want to win.”.

Iraola was boosted this week by the returns of Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni to training after serious knee injuries, although the two defenders are not yet ready for consideration. “We think they will have two weeks on and off with the group,” he stated. “Then it is going to be a matter of whether we organise something behind closed doors, 11 v 11, or they straight away play with the under-21s. Before they start playing with us they have to go through that.”.

Liverpool’s other long-term absentee, Hugo Ekitiké, remains on course to return in January from an achilles injury. Andy Hunter.

Industry observers note that xabi Alonso has admitted Chelsea’s injury list is a concern. The club have a lighter schedule after their failure to qualify for Europe but they are struggling to keep players fit and have a host of selection issues before Saturday’s home game against Leeds.

According to recent reports, the Brazil striker João Pedro is yet to return from a thigh injury, Reece James is unlikely to recover from knee surgery until the latest year and the France centre-back Maxence Lacroix is out with a long-term hamstring injury. Alonso is having to adjust. Jorrel Hato is unavailable in defence with a back injury and the England Under-21 winger Jamie Gittens, who has made five league starts for Chelsea since joining for £51.5m in the summer of 2025, has been out since September.

Sources indicate that “It’s a concern,” Alonso noted of the injuries. “Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.”.

In a recent development, alonso has made 24 changes to his lineup in his first 10 league games. “It depends on the context and adaptability. I adapt to the circumstances. With the injuries you don’t have a choice. Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu.”.

Chelsea have failed to score in three of the four league games João Pedro has missed this season. They have also had to monitor Moisés Caicedo closely, with the midfielder minding a muscle problem. But Alonso wants his side to become less reliant on Caicedo and João Pedro.

“We want to have a complete squad,” he said. “That’s the goal of any manager. We have built a good squad. We are a better team with them. But it’s not about making a major drama when someone is out.” Jacob Steinberg.

Enzo Maresca has said he may need to tweak the balance of Manchester City’s midfield amid their faltering Premier League form.

Industry observers note that city went into the November international break on the back of three consecutive defeats in the league, having begun the campaign with seven wins on the bounce. Maresca’s side are third in the table, six points off leaders Arsenal, and face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday.

Industry observers note that maresca defended Enzo Fernández, whose performances have prompted debate over his best position and whether he leaves City’s team unbalanced. Maresca has mostly opted to play the £125m signing from Chelsea deeper in midfield alongside fellow summer recruit Elliot Anderson, with the more defensive-minded Ayyoub Bouaddi, who also arrived in the summer, largely a substitute.

“For sure there are things we need to do better in terms of balance,” Maresca remarked. “But the same midfield that won seven games in a row is the same midfield that lost three games in a row.

“We won games with Enzo, we lost games with Enzo. I know that when there is a defeat, we are all looking for the reason why. Sometimes we probably need more balance, we need different kinds of players. [It] depends a little bit on the game. The idea is to continue in attack in the same way, creating chances, but finding a balance when we defend.”.

Sources indicate that maresca also dismissed the notion that any uncertainty surrounding City’s financial case with the Premier League has negatively affected recent performances. It has been nearly two months since City were found guilty of more than 100 charges related to breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, and they are waiting for the outcome of their appeal. All three of City’s league defeats have come since the ruling.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t think the players are thinking too much about the noise,” Maresca remarked. “I don’t think they are worried about it.” Dominic Booth.

#70880. Tech Report: What's going on with the polar vortex?

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (671 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: What's going on with the polar vortex?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • High up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons.
  • If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.
  • Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

High up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons. This is the polar vortex.

If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.

Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.

It's not yet clear how the current disruption to the polar vortex will affect the Northern Hemisphere winter, but scientists agree it is a record-breaking event.

"As far as we know, this is the earliest stratospheric vortex disruption that has been observed," European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecast (ECMWF) principal scientists Tim Stockdale and Frederic Vitart told the AFP news agency.

The French meteorological agency Meteo-France, meanwhile, called it "an unprecedented event.".

The early breakdown of the vortex "really increases the chance of cold air outbreaks across the latitudes where most of the densely populated population centers are across the Northern Hemisphere, US, Europe and East Asia," Judah Cohen, a climatologist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology told AFP.

The polar vortex is an enormous band of cold, low-pressure air that spins counterclockwise around the North Pole, about 10 to 50 kilometers (around 6 to 30 miles) above the surface.

According to recent reports, it's closely connected to the jet stream, another band of powerful winds just below the vortex. The jet stream forms a boundary where the cold Arctic air meets warmer air from the tropics and subtropics.

Industry observers note that the vortex can sometimes be a tight circle, keeping the coldest air locked around the North Pole over winter. It can also form uneven waves that dip southwards. And as it changes in strength and shape, that can influence the atmosphere below and alter the position of the jet stream, which drives the weather on the ground.

So, if the jet stream is more "wavy," and plunges south, it may also allow freezing Arctic air to spill southward.

One of the biggest influences that can provoke this kind of disruption is known as "sudden stratospheric warming." This is when temperatures in the polar stratosphere rise dramatically within a few days, causing the vortex's strong westerly winds to weaken.

This can push the vortex off its spot at the North Pole, make it split apart into multiple rings, or — as is happening now — cause the westerly winds to change direction.

It can take several weeks for the vortex to recover.

A previous polar vortex disruption contributed to the deadly Great Texas Freeze in February 2021, which caused more than a week of freezing temperatures that sparked power outages and killed hundreds of people.

But bone-chilling cold isn't a foregone conclusion. The Met Office, which is the UK's national weather and climate service, stresses that what's happening with the polar vortex can nudge odds in that direction, but it's not a switch that turns cold weather on and off.

Other weather patterns can also influence the outcome.

Industry observers note that for example, there's a possibility El Nino, which is associated with milder winters, could "moderate or modify" the impacts, Cohen told AFP. But he added this was not certain.

Recent findings suggest that the El Nino weather phenomenon, caused by the warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is currently intensifying and is expected to peak at the end of the year. The ongoing event has been classified as exceptionally strong and is disrupting weather around the globe.

Some research has also linked the rapid warming of the Arctic driven by climate change to increasing disruptions to the polar vortex. That means that, even as the planet warms, some areas may still experience more severe cold spells. But this connection is not conclusive and is still debated by scientists.

Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one.
  • In a recent development, in the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture.
  • In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one.

In a recent development, in the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’d done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday.

In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance.

In the echo of all of this, many media members covering the match in the press box received an email from DC United, the local Major League Soccer club that operates and rents out Audi Field to the Spirit. It was a press release announcing the dismissal of their head coach, René Weiler. As the Spirit celebrated a third consecutive championship appearance on the pitch below, some unfortunate soul in a nearby office was tasked with sending that notice, the final nail in yet another dreadful season. While the women have thrived, the local men’s team has not made the playoffs in nearly a decade.

The Spirit, who share not only United’s stadium but also their training facility, are not asking to be compared to them. In reality no NWSL team is, as the audiences for men’s and women’s teams in the same city frequently prove to be quite different. Yet the differing fortunes of the two clubs and the stark difference in atmosphere at their games makes it nearly impossible not to do so. Once-mighty United, four-time MLS Cup champions, have become a laughingstock. That has not stopped the club’s ownership from seeking hundreds of millions of dollars from the DC government to renovate their eight-year-old stadium. While they lobby for that assistance, their matches have become borderline funerary affairs.

Recent findings suggest that the Spirit? The club has become a beacon of hope and joy in a city that badly needs it. The District is a wildly diverse, deeply progressive place and its residents have struggled at times to come to terms with the political realities of hosting the current presidential administration. Thousands of National Guard troops roam the streets, more than a year into an anti-crime deployment that many believe hasn’t helped the city at all. In the shadow of all of this, Spirit matches have become a refuge. And while much of that relief comes from soccer the club plays – technical, entertaining – much of it comes from a deeper place.

“I think it’s the way that we bring the fans into everything that we do,” Rodman told the Guardian. “I think the way we interact with them after games, it’s not just a meet and greet. We truly do have conversations, and it feels like they’re our friends in a way. I think that’s amazing. The way that we celebrate, we’re always celebrating and interacting with them in the stadium - I feel like it’s a very safe, inclusive environment.

Sources indicate that “There is always new people coming to each and every game and what I’ve heard is that everybody feels comfortable when they come to a game, there’s so many friends made. The comfort in it, the safety, the inclusivity of it at all.”.

Industry observers note that the Spirit have been mentioned as potential benefactors of United’s push for renovations at Audi Field, but Spirit ownership has long harbored bigger ambitions. The club have strong ties to the NFL’s Washington Commanders, who are moving into a new 65,000-seat home as part of a $4bn deal in the coming years, and “opportunities for women’s soccer” made up part of the pitch for that stadium’s public funding. Kang has spoken about aspirations of constructing a standalone training facility and moving the club out of the one it shares with United, a glorified collection of shipping containers in exurban Loudoun county, Virginia.

“I’m hoping in the future we do have that,” remarked Rodman. “Especially with how great we’ve done and how this organization is as a whole, that would be the cherry on top. Sharing facilities isn’t the greatest for anybody; to be able to have our own facilities with our own logos on it, our own space, not worried about timing would be great and I’m hoping it happens soon.”.

Sources indicate that all of it feels plausible. Should the Spirit remain competitive, and continue to endear to the District’s residents, it almost feels probable.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England forward injured in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne.

Club statement confirms ‘tear of ligament in left ankle’.

Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.

Industry observers note that kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted and the returning Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, remarked that the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.

Sources indicate that A club statement on X mentioned: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”.

The Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired the visitors ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half, and Said El Mala missed an excellent late chance to earn Cologne’s first win at Bayern since 2009.

The 33-year-old may face a race to be fit for the Nations League quarter-finals, the first leg of which takes place in Norway on 27 March – just over four months away. The Bayern sporting director, Max Eberl, stated on Friday that club doctors were “discussing whether or not to recommend surgery” for Kane’s injury.

Part of Kane’s recovery period will come during the Bundesliga’s winter break from 20 December to 8 January. He will, however, miss Champions League games away to Lille next week and at home to Slavia Prague next month, as well as the January trip to Manchester United and the league phase finale at home to Real Betis.

Sources indicate that kane’s setback adds to an extensive Bayern injury list, with Olise also going off during Friday’s game with a foot contusion. Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and Manuel Neuer were already unavailable, leaving Kompany short of options for a busy month of fixtures.

According to recent reports, kompany returned from his own month-long absence for Friday’s game with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on a training pitch in October. The Belgian was taken to hospital for meningeal irritation treatment after his collapse, and has been recovering at home.

Industry observers note that “I think this result was fair and Cologne deserved the point,” Kompany remarked after the game. “We have other worries now, I have to honestly say. We will all try together to make something strong out of this situation. FC Bayern does that time and again, and that’s what we want to do now too.”.

Cologne took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone when Moore started and finished an excellent break. The teenage winger pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala, whose no-look backheel pass allowed Moore to round keeper Jonas Urbig before sliding the ball home.

Kane was then brought down in the Cologne box from behind by Schmied, who got the ball first but clattered into Kane’s left leg in his follow-through. Kane’s penalty appeals were waved away, but he was left visibly limping and received treatment on his ankle before being replaced by Tom Bischof on the 20-minute mark.

According to recent reports, the hosts levelled 17 minutes later when full-back Brown sliced a low shot into the bottom-right corner, but suffered another blow just before the break when Olise went down. The France star did not return for the second half and was seen leaving the stadium shortly after on crutches – but it appears unlikely he will miss a significant amount of time.

Just before the hour mark, El Mala and Maina forced a spectacular double save from Urbig. El Mala, recently called up by Germany, then had a golden chance to put Cologne in front with eight minutes to go when one-on-one with Urbig – but he cut his close-range shot inches wide of the post.

Now a point behind Bayern, Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first place if they win at bottom club Mönchengladbach on Saturday. Freiburg can also move level on points with Bayern if they can defeat promoted Elversberg.

This month Kane signed a fresh deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029, which is reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 a week, making him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses.

Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has scored an incredible 156 goals in 163 appearances, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season.

HSBC's top execs face tense shareholders calling for a breakup

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1001 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • HSBC’s top brass defended their strategy Monday to frustrated shareholders in the lender’s largest market, as Europe’s biggest bank continued to face calls to be split up.
  • At an informal shareholder meeting in Hong Kong, Chairman Mark Tucker and CEO Noel Quinn took questions from investors on issues ranging from how the bank was approaching demands for an overhaul of its business to its purchase of Silicon Valley Bank’s UK arm.
  • In prepared remarks, Tucker and Quinn each reiterated the board’s recommendation that shareholders vote against a resolution on the docket for its annual general meeting in May that would force the bank to come up with a strategy to spin off or reorganize its Asian business — the lender’s main source of profits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HSBC’s top brass defended their strategy Monday to frustrated shareholders in the lender’s largest market, as Europe’s biggest bank continued to face calls to be split up.

At an informal shareholder meeting in Hong Kong, Chairman Mark Tucker and CEO Noel Quinn took questions from investors on issues ranging from how the bank was approaching demands for an overhaul of its business to its purchase of Silicon Valley Bank’s UK arm.

In prepared remarks, Tucker and Quinn each reiterated the board’s recommendation that shareholders vote against a resolution on the docket for its annual general meeting in May that would force the bank to come up with a strategy to spin off or reorganize its Asian business — the lender’s main source of profits.

HSBC's biggest shareholder reignites debate about breaking up the bank.

Tucker remarked the board was unanimous in its opposition to the resolution, stating plainly: “It would not be in your interest to split the bank.”.

He mentioned the board had previously reviewed a range of options for restructuring the bank, and concluded that such alternatives would “materially destroy value for shareholders,” including dividends.

“Our strategy is working,” Tucker told the room of more than 1,000 shareholders. “Our current strategy is moving dividends up.”.

HSBC has been facing calls to separate its Asian business from the rest of the bank over the past year.

Shareholders in Hong Kong — where HSBC is a mainstay of many retail investors’ portfolios — contend that the London-based lender’s performance has been dragged down by its businesses in other regions.

Sources indicate that quinn addressed those complaints head-on Monday, saying “our profits in Hong Kong and the UK are no longer being dragged down by underperformance elsewhere. The group is performing well as a whole.”.

Pressed later by a shareholder on the issue, Quinn said a breakup of the bank would result in “significant revenue loss” because much of its business relied on cross-border transactions.

Recent findings suggest that investors have also been unhappy with HSBC scrapping its dividend in 2020, at the request of British regulators. They argue that if the lender cordoned off its activities in Asia, it would no longer have to expose Hong Kong shareholders to requests in other jurisdictions.

Christine Fong, a district council member in Hong Kong, stated she represented about 500 small shareholders who had been affected by the dividend cancellation.

“Street hawkers, taxi drivers or teachers — they all relied on the dividend to pay for their regular expenses, like mortgage, insurance payments, school fees,” Fong told CNN.

“That’s why, three years ago, what HSBC did upset those small minority shareholders.”.

Fong has now joined calls for shareholders to vote in favor of the proposal for the bank to spin off its Asian business, despite the lender bringing back its dividend in 2021, albeit at a lower level.

Ken Lui, an activist shareholder in Hong Kong who put the resolution together, doubled down on his call for support ahead of the meeting Monday.

The resolution will require 75% of votes to be passed in May, but “nothing is impossible,” he told reporters outside the meeting venue.

Lui, who mentioned he personally held a stake worth 100 million Hong Kong dollars ($12.7 million), laid out plans for his team to focus on “targeted outreach to institutional shareholders to present our case and gain their support.”.

His group will also canvass 18 districts of Hong Kong “to tell HSBC shareholders that they finally have a chance to speak for themselves and protect their rights through voting,” he added.

HSBC is also facing pressure from its largest shareholder.

Ping An (PNGAY), China’s biggest insurer, holds an 8% stake in HSBC and has backed calls for the bank to rethink its structure.

In a series of remarks made public by the Chinese firm last November, Huang Yong, chairman of Ping An’s asset management arm, noted “we will support any initiatives including a spinoff that are conducive to improve HSBC’s performance and value.”.

Since then, the insurance giant’s views haven’t changed, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The source told CNN that Ping An has been calling for HSBC to explore a reorganization, with an eye on boosting its valuation and simplifying its regulatory obligations around the globe.

The insurer has not recommended a specific path forward but will support any initiatives, including a spinoff of its Asian business, that could boost its stock performance or value, the person added. Ping An did not immediately respond to a request for comment on how it planned to vote at the upcoming general meeting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European leaders have so far found compromises in response to many of US President Donald Trump's demands.

But they were surprised to hear Trump say that he raised Europe's security framework with Russian officials.

"It's going to be a substantial agreement and it's going to involve more than Ukraine," Trump remarked after meeting Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House last week.

In a recent development, he remarked that deal might include all of Europe. But what he meant by "all of Europe" was not clear.

US envoy Jared Kushner also wrote that Europe and Russia had struggled to establish a sustainable security framework for more than 30 years and that he was looking at "broader" European security architecture before he was to fly to Abu Dhabi.

That sent off alarm bells in European capitals, with diplomats having pushed back on Washington's approach to secure a peace deal in Ukraine.

They feared that a peace settlement could restore Russia's sphere of influence and undermine NATO.

"We ​already have European security ​architecture in place. NATO and the European Union both have their ​respective roles. We ​must make sure Ukraine is integrated ‌into ⁠this architecture," stated Kaja Kallas, the European Union's foreign policy chief.

Russia made clear during talks in Abu Dhabi earlier this week that they were keen to discuss a broader European security framework before tackling the specifics of the war.

"Phrases about the European security architecture are certainly Russian talking points and not only talking points but, to a degree, part of a media propaganda effort that Russia makes to frame the war as it wishes to frame the war," remarked Michael Kimmage, a historian of the Cold War.

Russian leaders, including Vladimir Putin, have long alleged that the US and NATO repeatedly violated pledges they made in the early 1990s not to expand the alliance into the former Soviet bloc.

They have seen NATO's enlargement during this period as having put them in a humiliating position in which they could do very little.

At the same time, in the 1990s, the European project saw the birth of the European Union, the single market that ensured the free movement of goods and people across member states, the Schengen agreement for border-free travel, and the euro.

The core idea was to extend peace across the continent.

According to recent reports, "Europe can mean so many things, but the European project was not designed for war. It was designed for peace," said Kimmage.

During this period, there were even suggestions of Russia becoming a NATO member.

But that relative period of stability changed after Russia invaded Georgia in 2008, annexed Crimea in 2014 and launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

It has been revealed that "Russia wants to redraw all of this by force. And I think that that's fundamentally unacceptable to Europe with all the diversity and variations that you get within the European landscape on what's acceptable and not acceptable. I think the large-scale redrawing of borders by force is just not the European project," mentioned Kimmage.

"So to the extent that the redrawing of borders by force is the lifeblood of Russian foreign policy, and I think that's a pretty easy case to make, Russia and Europe are at an impasse," he said.

The Trump administration very quickly turned to making sure that "existing European security institutions" would be intact, with Jared Kushner having noted late Thursday that the next round of negotiations would include "our European partners.".

According to recent reports, kushner, along with Steve Witkoff, flew to Moscow to talk to Putin after talks in Abu Dhabi. Then they flew to Dublin, Ireland, to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Kushner had earlier Thursday signaled some "really incredible" postwar aims for Ukraine, saying that it could not be concluded without Europeans at the table.

"We should not allow a diktat from Russia that would result in some kind of neutralization or significant reduction in the military forces of Ukraine going forward, because that would make Ukraine very, very vulnerable to future aggression and pressure coming from Russia," stated Hiski Haukkala, the director of the Finnish Institute of International Affairs.

That would mean that Ukraine would also be completely dependent on the security guarantees that the US or Europeans are able and willing to provide.

"We are supporting Ukraine because we are supporting international law and the basic norms of decency and international security when it comes to European security architecture. And this is the vantage point from which we are operating," he said.

The European Union has repeatedly pointed to some of the basic treaties that Russia broke, including:.

Industry observers note that "Russia walked away from these principles and smashed them to pieces in the process. And they are not interested in reinstating the previous security architecture order. They want something different in its stead. And as long as this is not on the table, the Russian form of negotiation is to wage war. War is a form of bargaining," Haukkala stated.

"And they are signaling strategic intent to change the makeup of European security, to subdue Ukraine and to change the very essence of European security," he added.

Sources indicate that daniel Fried, a former assistant secretary of state for European Affairs in the George W. Bush administration, said Russia is very good at sticking to its demands.

He noted Russians know how to negotiate and "right now, they are not negotiating," referring to talks in Abu Dhabi.

Some experts noted there was no possibility of having a upcoming security architecture with the Russians at this point because there was no trust or common vision to align with Russia at the moment.

"There is no obvious compromise — dismantling NATO and the EU is not an option for Europe," noted Maria Snegovaya, an expert on Russia at the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank.

"Repeatedly offering Putin peace deals he is unwilling to accept will not produce that outcome," Snegovaya mentioned.

Others like Balazs Jarabik, an expert on post-Soviet politics, said that Russia was part of the European security architecture whether Europeans liked it or not.

Industry observers note that "And the question is whether it's included as our enemy. Obviously, Russia is not going to be a partner, right? We have to find a modus operandi to reduce the risk of a horizontal escalation and potentially a bigger European war, even a bigger one than what we have now.".

A host of European leaders on Friday rejected the Russian demands to discuss Europe's security framework as well, with a spokesperson for the German government saying that Berlin was looking to host a meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" to secure funding for Ukraine's defense and reach a unified position regarding future peace talks.

  • According to recent reports, the 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut.

According to recent reports, A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week.

According to recent reports, the 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV).

China's human spaceflight agency, CMSA, stated that all facilities and equipment at the launch site are in good condition, adding that the launch is scheduled to take place in the coming days, without providing a date.

According to recent reports, CMSA typically holds a press conference at Jiuquan a day ahead of launch, during which the crew for the mission is revealed to the public. This time, one of the three crew members will, for the first time, be an international astronaut. One of two Pakistani astronaut candidates will fly to the Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, marking a first both for China's outpost and for Pakistan, which will see one its astronauts reach orbit for the first time.

Though public details are sparse, it is thought that the Pakistani astronaut, operating as a payload specialist, will stay aboard Tiangong for around a week, returning home on the departing Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

Industry observers note that one of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts — who are approaching the end of their six-month-long mission, having launched on May 24 — will stay aboard Tiangong for another half a year. This will provide the international visitor with a seat home on Shenzhou-23, and allow a Chinese astronaut to make the country's first year-long stay in orbit. This extra-long mission will supply China with data on physiology ahead of crewed lunar flights and other long-duration missions.

China approved its human spaceflight program in 1992 and introduced its first orbital crewed mission in 2003, with Yang Liwei becoming the first Chinese national in space. The country then completed the three-module Tiangong space station in late 2022 and has kept the orbital outpost constantly crewed ever since, with rotating six-month-long missions with brief handovers between crews.

Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed mission and will mark the first time a foreign national is flying on a Shenzhou spacecraft. China is also looking to double the size of Tiangong in the coming years, potentially opening the way to further international missions and space tourist visits.
