  • After the makeup brand’s founder Huda Kattan apologized to the beauty influencer for how her firm handled discontinuing their darkest setting powder Coffee Cake and replacing it with Coco Truffle, Golloria shared her thoughts on the response.
  • Sources indicate that “I appreciate your apology and you taking the time to get back to me,” Golloria posted in the comments of Kattan’s Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Golloria can’t conceal her thoughts on Huda Beauty’s apology.

After the makeup brand’s founder Huda Kattan apologized to the beauty influencer for how her firm handled discontinuing their darkest setting powder Coffee Cake and replacing it with Coco Truffle, Golloria shared her thoughts on the response.

Sources indicate that “I appreciate your apology and you taking the time to get back to me,” Golloria posted in the comments of Kattan’s Nov. 20 Instagram post. “Speaking from both my experience as a shade consultant and as a dark skinned woman whose shade options are directly affected by this decision, I don’t think Coco Truffle should replace Coffee Cake. And that’s just the honest truth.”.

The TikToker explained that she heard Huda Beauty’s reasoning that Coffee Cake wasn’t doing well with consumers, but added that she didn’t think the two shades were “interchangeable,” noting that “a shade occupying a similar depth in a range doesn’t necessarily mean it serves the same complexions.”.

Industry observers note that “You’ve remarked several times that you want to better serve dark skinned women, and part of that is listening to the women telling you that Coffee Cake already works for them,” the 25-year-old continued. “That feedback should help guide what you preserve as you expand the range.”.

She also added that darker skinned women “deserve variety in both depth and undertone,” and that having both shades would help create that inclusion. Instead, Golloria shared in her own Instagram caption that she felt Huda Beauty was “doing what's easiest for the brand instead of what's needed by the women you say you want to serve.”.

“Inclusion means making room for our differences,” she wrote, “not asking us to settle for whatever is most convenient for you to offer.”.

As for Kattan, while the beauty founder did not reply to Golloria’s comment, she explained in her apology video that she was sorry for how the conversation about the shade replacement had been handled with Golloria, especially as it was happening during a busy time for the brand and when Kattan herself had to undergo emergency surgery for a ruptured breast implant in April.

According to the 43-year-old, her team found that Coffee Cake was “not something that a lot of people have shared positive feedback with us on,” adding that they “definitely thought we could make it a lot better.”.

The decision led them to launching Coco Truffle as a replacement for Coffee Cake, first as a pressed powder, then as a loose powder—although it was not yet widely available.. But after hearing from their consumers, Kattan realized they should have done a better job being more inclusive with their shades.

“Inclusivity is not about, ‘Yes, done, check, we're inclusive.’ That to me is some of the things that are wrong with the industry,” she said. “It's 2026. We can do better. We can do better and I think brands should be doing better in 2026.”.

And while they will be reworking Coco Truffle to make sure it’s available “as promptly as possible,” she also regretted fully removing Coffee Cake from their lineup.

“We should have kept it in stores,” Kattan stated, “because at the end of the day, if some people liked it, we should have kept it in stores until there was something better available.”.

She also once again apologized for not having better communicated all of this to Golloria initially, although she was hopeful that the beauty influencer and Huda Beauty fans would appreciate Coco Truffle.

“I'm hoping to give you guys a shade that you guys really, really love, and all the beautiful rich skin tone girls and boys feel really represents them,” Kattan shared, “and is perfect for their skin tone.”.

Breaking: The Smart Ring Goes to Church

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that stressed?
  • Industry observers note that the first generation of Christian smart rings is here, joining other religious wearables like iQibla’s dedicated Muslim smartwatches, rings, and Hajj bands alongside “kosher” smartwatch apps.
  • Everblessed’s $249 Elah Ring S1 went on sale in October and is shipping in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that stressed? Heart rate elevated? If you’re wearing a smart ring from Oura, Ultrahuman, or Samsung, the spike could prompt app suggestions like breathing exercises, meditations, or a physical reset like a short walk. So far, so Silicon Valley. But now you can add reading the Bible to that list of self-soothing activities.

Industry observers note that the first generation of Christian smart rings is here, joining other religious wearables like iQibla’s dedicated Muslim smartwatches, rings, and Hajj bands alongside “kosher” smartwatch apps. Two latest devices in particular—Glorify’s Ring and Everblessed Technology’s Elah Ring—connect to hugely popular Christian prayer apps with tens of millions of owners, and both claim to be the world’s first Christian smart ring.

Both are first, in their own ways. Everblessed’s $249 Elah Ring S1 went on sale in October and is shipping in the US. The $299 Glorify Ring launched in July, with reservations open and shipping set for January 2027, but 77,000 units of an earlier beta iteration, the Amen Ring made by faith tech organization ConfideIn (which merged with Glorify this May), were given away last Christmas. Everblessed manages the Blessed app, and Glorify has an eponymous app.

In a recent development, another big player in prayer apps is Hallow, aimed at Catholics, backed by Vice President JD Vance’s Narya venture capital firm and celebrity ambassadors, with 24 million installs to date. Hallow’s toe-dip into wearables was a 2024 smart rosary with NFC embedded in the crucifix, made with Italian brand Ghirelli; Everblessed tried an earbud, necklace, and bedside device before settling on the ring design.

Head-to-head on design, the Elah and Glorify rings are both made from titanium alloy, with a thorn-inspired twist for Glorify and a minimalist band featuring a cross for the Elah S1, which is also IP68 waterproof to 5 meters.

In a recent development, for now, the Elah Ring is slightly techier: prayer reminders come via the cross, which glows via an LED, and “gentle” vibrations; these can pulse at certain times of day or be triggered by changes in heart rate and stress levels, picked up by a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor. Glorify’s CEO Henry Costa tells WIRED these emotion-based reminders will land on the Glorify Ring in six months; for now, you can set the times of day you want prayer reminders, track heart rate, blood oxygen, stress, and sleep via the optical sensor.

Sources indicate that one addition to the Glorify Ring that Costa says he personally uses “a lot” is recording prayers straight into the built-in mic. The ring has a light to signal when it's recording, and the app transcribes them. Everblessed CEO Ricky Xia says that, after consulting with pastors and consumers, the feeling was that voice notes on the ring were seen as “suspicious.” It’s available in-app, but most people don’t pray out loud, and too many features drain the battery life. (The Elah Ring runs for up to six days on one charge; Glorify for four to five days.).

Both companies see the smart ring nudges helping wearers prioritize meaningful quiet time, away from screens, while offering in-app Christian practices as an alternative to Eastern meditation. Glorify offers Bible study, courses, and meditations. Blessed has devotional “anchors,” Bible texts and audio, plus guided breathing. Xia claims he’s happy if the Elah vibrates and a user picks up a paper Bible rather than the Blessed app, while Costa says he’s “crying out to use my phone less.”.

In a recent development, both Glorify (founded in 2020, now merged with ConfideIn and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area) and Blessed (founded in 2023 and based in San Jose) operate in more than 150 countries. Perhaps the biggest difference between the two rings is their relationship to AI.

Xia is all-in, describing the S1 as an “AI-native” product, with a pastor-complementing, not-replacing FaithMate chatbot in the Blessed app, customized based on preferences, congregation, and depth of learning. ChatGPT is like a “good coworker,” he says, while FaithMate is designed to be “your friend” and an agent that can also handle secular tasks.

“A lot of our users not only ask questions about the Bible but also ask about themselves, their relationships with their wives, they’re being bullied at school," Xia says, stressing safeguards around data storage, encryption, and privacy. "Everyone is going to have some AI that they trust, and how they view that is built on their personal stuff, their private vulnerabilities.”.

According to recent reports, costa is more circumspect, treading carefully on the consumer-facing side and noting that the Pope has weighed in with a 6,000-word encyclical on AI. A launch interview with CBN News garnered negative comments: “AI is Antichrist Information,” for one.

Recent findings suggest that “The stance I’ve always taken is that our daily devotional is hand-authored by a team of theologians,” Costa notes. “It’s prayed over, and that is a stamp of approval.” He criticizes AI slop prayer apps as inauthentic. Still, he says the Glorify team has already tested “many forms” of AI personalization: “Any time, if we do use AI, it must be very clear to the user.”.

Smart ring owners were finding ways to add faith features to mainstream accessories before these rings came to fruition. For 20 years, timer and reminder apps have helped with prayer schedules, but recent examples are more creative. Heidi Campbell, professor of communication in religious studies at Texas A&M, refers to these DIY upgrades to the Oura ring and devices like the Muse headband as “spiritual mind-body hacking.”.

Oura owners on #christiantiktok chat about how they already use the ring’s stress and HR alerts as a prompt to pause and reflect, as per Elah.

Smart ring users flag changes in resting heart rate and sleep quality with scripture following their daily practice. “It’s really helpful for, like, what was inhibiting me from getting to a meditative or contemplative prayer state?” Campbell indicates. “It takes some of the mystery out of prayer, I think, but that can also be positive. There is a way to do prayer well and not well.” Ring hackers can also dig into health stats during Lent, Ramadan, and Yom Kippur to analyze energy expenditure and how fasting periods affect their bodies.

AI-powered voice recordings and emerging attempts at emotion tracking are part of a newly introduced phase for smart rings, notes Ekta Mittal, a senior analyst of connected devices at CCS Insight. These new “purpose-driven” features extend wearable tech into “new parts of consumers’ daily routines,” Mittal says. She suggests that while Glorify and Everblessed will add value for some, the rings are “not directly competing” with established smart ring giants like Oura, Ultrahuman, and Samsung.

It has been revealed that the pandemic sped up the digital transition of many places of worship when congregations could not meet up in person, encouraging experimentation with social media. So it’s early days for Silicon Valley’s impact on organized religion. Researchers at the University of Würzburg in Germany, led by Ilona Nord, are studying the theological implications of using tech, including smart rings, for spiritual practices, investigating which values are baked into secular devices and apps.

Campbell suggests many Christian groups haven’t stopped to consider the unintentional consequences of cultivating spirituality via personal tech. “All of these things are about individualizing the practice, which is good, but the challenges are for religions which are really focused on communal aspects,” she says. Not everyone has the money or connectivity to access these gadgets, but also, more existentially, “it puts spiritual development over communal development.”.

Xia points to the Blessed app’s communities, including its Healing Room broadcast feature, which lets pastors go live with sermons. It's not in the Elah app yet, but it's on the roadmap. Costa states communal practice is a core pillar, highlighting the “social layer” of public notes made on Christian texts in-app and an upcoming Glorify Ring feature which will allow a user to pair their device with a family member’s ring: “When your loved one is feeling down, you’ll get a buzz to check in with them.”.

Celtic 4-1 St Mirren; Rangers 2-1 Motherwell.

Sources indicate that “It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet. But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.”.

In a recent development, steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and Dundee’s performance, saying: “It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

“I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that. We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and shows grit. We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that. I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.”.

The recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1. The champions brushed off the loss of midfield pair Mika Baur and Benjamin Nygren to injury to consolidate their place at the top of the Premiership.

In a recent development, the centre-forward Camilo Duran was also on target as Celtic killed the game late in the first half with three goals in nine minutes. Callum McGregor grabbed his first league goal of the season before Killian Phillips scored a consolation from the spot.

With Baur facing up to 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Nygren nursing a heel problem, Martin O’Neill would have been delighted with how his midfield functioned.

Sources indicate that oxlade-Chamberlain made his fifth start of the season and McCowan his second. The pair had never started a game together before. O’Neill also introduced the former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joël van den Berg for a debut in the second half and the 19-year-old revealed some good touches.

Ryan Naderi hit a deflected 88th-minute winner at Fir Park as Rangers stayed four points behind Celtic by beating Motherwell 2-1. Naderi’s effort went in off the unfortunate Motherwell defender Martin Moorman as Rangers finally made the most of some late pressure to win.

In a recent development, the visitors looked as if they might be held to a third draw in four away games after Jake Girdwood-Reich had cancelled out an early opener from Rangers defender Emmanuel Fernandez. Rangers had 29 shots at goal but found Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen in top form and the Newly introduced Zealand international pulled off one of the saves of the season to deny Dujon Sterling with five minutes left.

However, they netted after a corner when Naderi’s shot from eight yards went in off Moorman after the Austrian had blocked a shot from Badredine Bouanani.

It has been revealed that mario Frick enjoyed a dream start to life as Aberdeen manager by edging a six-goal thriller with a 4-2 win at Kilmarnock. Kevin Nisbet’s double along with Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall strikes secured three priceless points to leave the Rugby Park side rooted to the bottom.

The visitors climbed to eighth spot after a remarkable afternoon where the Pittodrie side hit a much-needed scoring streak. Aberdeen opted to dispense with the services of Stephen Robinson after a run of one win from seven which saw them sink to second bottom and Frick was appointed as his replacement last Sunday.

According to recent reports, dundee United recorded their biggest ever win at Easter Road with an impressive 4-0 thrashing of Hibernian. Zac Sapsford’s first-half double laid the foundations before Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall found the net after the break.

It has been revealed that the visitors were well worth the three points as they cemented their place in the top six and picked up their first win in Leith since 2021. It was a humbling afternoon for Hibs, who thought they had turned a corner under their new head coach, Marink Reedijk, after back-to-back victories before the international break.

It has been revealed that falkirk clung on to clock up six top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1966 with a 2-1 home victory against St Johnstone. John McGlynn’s team scored early in each half to remain third.

Recent findings suggest that jacob Murrell’s eighth goal of a superb debut season sent Falkirk on their way inside six minutes. Finley Barbrook’s second goal in as many games on 48 minutes doubled the advantage. Josh Campbell nodded in a late reply to serve up a scare but the hosts held firm.

#70769. Scientists discover a bizarre paradox among endangered penguins

Scientists discover a bizarre paradox among endangered penguins

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1253 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A upcoming study from the University of Otago, Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka, has revealed a surprising divide in the fortunes of one of New Zealand's least understood penguin species.
  • Published in PLOS ONE, the research found that one population has remained stable for at least 25 years, while the other has declined by more than 40 percent over the past three decades.
  • Thomas Mattern of the Tawaki Project, which brings together scientists from the university's Departments of Zoology and Marine Science.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A upcoming study from the University of Otago, Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka, has revealed a surprising divide in the fortunes of one of New Zealand's least understood penguin species. Although Erect-crested penguins breed in just two remote island groups, their populations are experiencing dramatically different outcomes.

Published in PLOS ONE, the research found that one population has remained stable for at least 25 years, while the other has declined by more than 40 percent over the past three decades.

The study was led by Dr. Thomas Mattern of the Tawaki Project, which brings together scientists from the university's Departments of Zoology and Marine Science. Researchers also collaborated with the Antarctic Research Trust and the Global Penguin Society.

Drone Surveys Reveal a Surprising Penguin Population Divide.

Erect-crested penguins breed exclusively on the Bounty and Antipodes islands, two isolated island groups located approximately 800 kilometers southeast of New Zealand's South Island.

Sources indicate that to determine how many penguins remain, researchers conducted extensive drone surveys between 2022 and 2024. They photographed and counted every breeding colony across both island groups, producing the first comprehensive population survey of the entire species.

"The results overturn a long-standing assumption," Dr. Mattern states.

"The tiny Bounty Islands, at just 50 hectares, were found to hold almost as many breeding pairs (about 27,800) as the Antipodes Islands (about 29,800), even though the latter is 40 times larger and historically considered the species' stronghold.".

The difference in population trends was even more unexpected. Despite their small size, the Bounty Islands have maintained a relatively consistent number of breeding penguins for decades. Meanwhile, the much larger Antipodes Islands have experienced a substantial decline.

"Comparing the new counts with historical records going back to the mid-1990s, the Bounty Islands population has remained essentially unchanged for at least 25 years.

"The Antipodes Islands population, by contrast, has declined by more than 40 percent since 1995.".

Why Are Penguins Disappearing From the Antipodes Islands?

Sources indicate that researchers believe several overlapping pressures may explain why the two populations are heading in opposite directions. Natural predators, increasingly destructive storms, and differences in where the birds travel and feed could all be contributing.

In a recent development, one particularly troubling factor involves skuas, native subantarctic birds that prey on penguin eggs and chicks. As penguin colonies become smaller, the birds lose some of the protection that comes from nesting together in large numbers.

"As Antipodes colonies have shrunk over recent decades, the collective defense they once provided against native subantarctic bird, the skua, a natural predator of eggs and chicks, has weakened, allowing predation losses to increase and colonies to fragment further.".

According to recent reports, co-author Dr. Klemens Pütz of the Antarctic Research Trust suggests that changes involving another penguin species may have intensified this pressure.

Recent findings suggest that eastern Rockhopper penguins suffered a "catastrophically" severe population collapse during the second half of the 20th century. Similar declines occurred across their Southern Ocean breeding range, likely driven by warming ocean waters. Today, fewer than 1,000 breeding pairs remain on the Antipodes Islands.

"As Rockhoppers disappeared, skuas may have turned to Erect-crested penguin eggs and chicks instead," Dr. Pütz claims.

Stronger Storms and Different Migration Routes Add to the Threat.

In a recent development, predators are not the only challenge facing the Antipodes penguins. Increasingly powerful storms, consistent with wider climate trends across the Southern Ocean, have caused landslides that break up breeding colonies and leave the birds more vulnerable.

Differences in ocean habitats and seasonal movements may also help explain why the two populations have experienced such contrasting outcomes.

According to Dr. Mattern, penguins breeding on the Antipodes Islands migrate considerable distances into the Antarctic Polar Frontal Zone when the breeding season ends. In contrast, birds from the Bounty Islands remain closer to their nesting grounds, where the surrounding waters are more sheltered and may offer more abundant food.

These differences could leave the two populations exposed to very different environmental pressures, despite belonging to the same species.

The Strange Paradox of Schrödinger's Penguin.

The researchers have named this unusual situation "Schrödinger's Penguin," drawing inspiration from the famous physics thought experiment involving a cat inside a sealed box.

Industry observers note that in that experiment, the cat is imagined to be both alive and dead until the box is opened and its condition is observed. But Dr. Mattern explains that the penguin discovery turns the familiar concept around.

"With Schrödinger's cat, opening the box settles the question one way or the other.

"With Erect-crested penguins, it's the opposite. From a distance, without proper surveys, everyone assumed there was a single answer for the whole species.

"Once we actually opened the metaphorical box and looked, we found there wasn't one state at all, but two: stable on the Bounty Islands, declining on the Antipodes Islands.".

Sources indicate that in other words, looking at the species as a whole can conceal what is happening within individual populations. Only by examining both island groups separately did researchers uncover how dramatically their circumstances differ.

A Hidden Conservation Crisis for Endangered Penguins.

It has been revealed that the Erect-crested penguin is at the moment one of only four penguin species worldwide classified as "Endangered" on the International Union for Conservation of Nature Red List. Another New Zealand penguin, the hoiho/yellow-eyed penguin, shares that designation.

It has been revealed that however, the two species have received very different levels of attention. While the plight of the hoiho has attracted ongoing public interest and conservation efforts, the Erect-crested penguin has remained relatively overlooked.

Dr. Mattern explains that the species' current conservation classification relies on population estimates from the 1970s that were considerably inflated. When the upcoming survey results are considered, the "Endangered" designation remains broadly appropriate for the declining Antipodes population, but not for the stable Bounty Islands population.

This creates a difficult conservation dilemma. If the two populations are combined into a single assessment, the species' overall threat classification could actually improve, even though one population continues to decline sharply.

"Averaged across both populations, the global ranking would actually improve to "Vulnerable," masking the severity of the Antipodes decline, and downplaying how exposed the Bounty Islands, likely the species' last secure stronghold, are to industrial fishing.".

The researchers warn that a more favorable overall classification could create a misleading impression of security. Although the Bounty Islands population remains stable, it may still face significant threats, particularly from industrial fishing activity.

"A single, ostensibly improved threat ranking is like putting the lid back on Schrödinger's box, trading a convenient illusion for the stronger protection the Bounty Islands population actually needs," Dr. Mattern indicates.

According to recent reports, the findings highlight why conservation efforts must account for the circumstances of individual populations rather than relying exclusively on a species' global status. For Erect-crested penguins, recognizing the differences between the two island groups could be essential to protecting their future.

The study received funding from the Vontobel Foundation (Switzerland) through the Antarctic Research Trust and from the Global Penguin Society. The research was carried out under permits issued by the Fresh Zealand Department of Conservation.
